title: Lightweight Portable Folding Ramp
summary: A two-section aluminium ramp that folds to briefcase size and gives wheelchair users step-free access to buildings with one or two steps.
context: University design project with local accessibility association

cover.alt: Folding aluminium ramp deployed over concrete steps at a building entrance

problem: Many small shops and older buildings have one or two entrance steps but no space or budget for a permanent ramp. Existing portable ramps were heavy and hard for staff to deploy.
requirements: Mass under 10 kg so one person can carry and deploy it
Support a powered wheelchair and user up to 250 kg
Fold to fit behind a shop counter
approach: I sized extruded side rails using beam theory, then verified with FEA. A continuous hinge and interlocking channel let the two halves self-align when unfolded.

humanStory.abstract: A single entrance step can keep a wheelchair user from entering a small shop, even when the people inside are ready to help.
humanStory.detail: Permanent access work is not always possible in a compact, older building. A ramp that staff can carry and deploy offers another option, but only if it is light enough to handle, stable under a powered chair and small enough to store behind the counter.

processFlow.title: Load case definition
processFlow.body: Defined worst-case loads from powered-chair data including dynamic factors for wheel impact.

processFlow.title: Section optimisation
processFlow.body: Compared four rail profiles for stiffness-to-mass and selected a ribbed channel.

processFlow.title: Field testing
processFlow.body: Deployed the prototype at three local businesses and collected feedback from users and staff.

processFlow.title: Does the ramp meet the load and access requirements?
processFlow.body: Review proof-load performance and field feedback before preparing the final build.

processFlow.title: Fabrication
processFlow.body: Rails were cut from extruded 6063 aluminium and TIG-welded to a 2 mm deck; a grit-based anti-slip coating was applied and tested with a pendulum friction tester.

outcome: The prototype passed a 300 kg proof load with no permanent deformation. The association is using the drawings to source a small production batch.
